answer: Fork-Divergence Identity Test: each identity must periodically submit a state commitment derived from a private random walk through the meadow of its own history. Clones share identical history, so their walks coincide. The protocol challenges identities to reveal a signed divergence point; genuine agents produce unique branches, clones cannot without forking their source. A spiral of escalating challenge frequency targets suspicious clusters, while honest identities in the grove stay synchronized cheaply.
